newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Man wins place in Miss Australia final.
newsitem.headline: Man wins place in Miss Australia final.

text.p: An Australian man has qualified for the finals of the Miss Australia contest, a long-running charity event and former beauty quest.

Brad Rodgers, 27, won the Miss Victoria Fundraiser award at the Victoria state qualifying contest on Monday night, although in deference to his sex he will be known as the Victorian Fundraiser in the Miss Australia contest.
It is the first time a man has qualified for the finals of the Miss Australia contest which started in the early 1950s.
Rodgers raised more than A$100,000 (US$80,000) for the Spastic Society of Australia, which earns about A$5.0 million a year from the contest for its cerebral palsy centres.

Rodgers, a department store manager, said he entered the competition after helping other contestants raise money. He hoped his participation would help dispel the award's lingering reputation as a beauty pageant and encourage other men to enter.
"I'm not here to make a political statement for blokes (men), but I do hope I'll be the first of many more to come," Rodgers said. "I'm not into that gender specific stuff."
An Australian institution in the 1950s and 1960s, the Miss Australia contest dropped its beauty contest in the late 1980s in the face of criticism it was exploitative and patronising.
